[TiSASRec](https://jiachengli1995.github.io/files/wsdm20.pdf) provides the foundational mechanism: combine positional information with learned pairwise time-interval embeddings inside self-attention. Its temporal mechanism is relevant to BERT4Rec, although its original backbone is different. Recent work explores complementary approaches: [Parameter-Efficiently Leveraging Session Information (2025)](https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/abstract/document/10902109) proposes session tokens, session segment embeddings and temporal self-attention; [Multi-Scale Transformers (2026)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0306457325002596) combines attention for transient and stable interests with adaptive masking to reduce redundant interactions.

[HyTRec (2026 preprint)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.18283) explicitly separates stable preferences from short-term intent and introduces temporal updates to respond to interest drift. Its evidence concerns industrial, extremely long histories, so benefits should not be assumed for sparse Amazon sequences. These papers motivate learned temporal relevance, but do not establish that older purchases are irrelevant or repeated recent interactions always indicate stronger intent.

A compatible experimental hypothesis is to retain one bidirectional BERT4Rec network and add per-head learned biases from bucketed history time gaps, optionally controlled by a jointly trained content-dependent gate. Initialize the temporal contribution near zero and compare against position-only attention; unrestricted learned biases can represent useful older interactions without enforcing monotonic decay. This is a proposed adaptation, not a reported result. Preserve [BERT4Rec’s masked-target objective](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.06690), appended-mask inference and final nonpadding readout. Use observed timestamps only; assign the appended mask a consistent history-derived time reference rather than the unavailable next-event timestamp. Evaluate with the fixed macro validation HR@10 protocol.
